text:
Lady of heaven, Regent of earth, Empress of infernal marshes: receive this humble erring Christian; she longs to join your heavenly chosen though knowing she lacks such merit. The riches flowing from you, my Lady, exceed all my baseness. Without them no soul rises to heaven; I do not lie like minstrels: in this faith I wish to live and die.

Tell Your Son I seek his way. Ask him to erase my sins, to forgive me as Egyptian Mary or Theophilus the clerk, whose pact with the devil was pardoned through Your sweet smile's intercession. Preserve me from the ever-stirring demon, Virgin who conceived without stain the sacrament celebrated at Mass: in this faith I wish to live and die.

I am poor and old and know no sacred texts, but in the church where I go for aid I saw Eden painted with harps and lutes and Hell where the damned boil. One greatly frightens me; my eyes joyfully behold the other, the only truth I know. I dream of reaching that bliss one day, Lady to whom sinners must turn sincerely, promptly, faithfully: in this faith I wish to live and die.

Your holy pregnancy, worthy Virgin Princess, bore King Jesus, infinite and unceasing, who assumed our sad nature, left heaven and came to die for us, sacrificing youthful beauty. Such is our God. My soul confesses itself His: in this faith I wish to live and die.

translation.title: Ballad for Praying to Our Lady
